findings.quoted_text: Any material change to scope, assumptions, dependencies, technical requirements, or delivery sequence should be documented in writing. A change request may describe additional fees, revised dates, or other effects before the changed work begins.

Client may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice, subject to payment of fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date. Contractor may terminate only for Client's material breach under Section 12.1.

Any material change to scope, assumptions, dependencies, technical requirements, or delivery sequence should be documented in writing. A change request may describe additional fees, revised dates, or other effects before the changed work begins.
findings.explanation: The word "should" (rather than "shall") and "may describe" (rather than "shall state") make the change-order requirement softer than an obligation. This leaves room for the Client to argue that a change was informally requested and that you are expected to perform it, even though the fee language is permissive.
findings.suggested_change: Any material change to scope, assumptions, dependencies, technical requirements, or delivery sequence must be documented in a written change order signed by both parties. A change order shall specify any additional fees, revised dates, or other commercial effects, and no changed work shall begin until both parties have agreed to and signed the change order.

findings.quoted_text: Client may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice, subject to payment of fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date. Contractor may terminate only for Client's material breach under Section 12.1.
findings.explanation: Only the Client can walk away without cause. You are compensated for work already done, which limits the damage, but you still have no symmetric right to exit if the relationship is not working.
findings.suggested_change: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 20 days' written notice. Upon any termination, Client shall pay Contractor all fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date, plus any reasonable, documented, pre-approved costs incurred by Contractor in anticipation of the terminated work.

findings.explanation: You will be waiting 40 days after each invoice is issued before being paid, which is ten days longer than the usual 30-day benchmark and ties up your cash flow.
findings.suggested_change: Invoices are payable Net 30 from the date of receipt.

findings.explanation: This clause sets your payment terms at Net 40, meaning the client has 40 days from the invoice or delivery date to pay you. This is 10 days longer than the standard Net 30 window, which extends the time you go without getting paid.
findings.suggested_change: Payment period: Net 30. The Client shall pay all invoices within thirty (30) days of the invoice date or date of delivery, whichever is later, by wire transfer to the Contractor bank account identified in this Agreement.
